sections.title: Framework settings
sections.what: Hides the framework name from response headers, sends old league and dashboard addresses to the crews page, and applies security headers to every path.
sections.why: The comments say leagues were renamed to crews and an empty login address breaks the build.
sections.watch_out: Redirects are permanent, so once browsers have cached them, removing them later will not undo that for those users.

summary: Main Next.js settings: redirects for renamed pages, security headers on every page, and a guard against an empty login address.
purpose: Keep old links working and send browsers security instructions.
why: The comments say leagues became crews, and an empty login address makes the build fail.
how: 1) Clear an empty login address setting. 2) Set framework options. 3) Add permanent redirects for old league and dashboard links. 4) Attach security headers to all paths, with a flag for development.
inputs: Environment variables such as NODE_ENV and NEXTAUTH_URL.
outputs: A configuration object that Next.js reads when building and running.
risks: Permanent redirects are cached by browsers and are hard to undo for users. The header choice depends on the production flag, so a mistake can weaken security.
debug: If a page redirects unexpectedly, check the redirect list. If a security header is missing, check the production flag and the securityHeaders function.
